findings.reason: naming the launcher/scheduler owner up front makes the serving job reuse `nova_lane`'s rung and log contract instead of accreting a parallel launcher and a second `squeue` read.
findings.text: §6 deliverable A ("an sbatch script and a small status command") duplicates two existing owners: `scripts/nova_lane/run.sh` (the repository's general compute-lane launcher, which already selects a rung, records the job id/node/revision in the log, and refuses a `--test-only` estimate) and `imas_codex/remote/tunnel.py::discover_compute_node` / `discover_compute_node_local` (which already resolve a service job's node with `squeue -n <service_job_name> --format=%N`). The landed `scripts/playable_server/run.sh`, `status.sh` and `payload.sh` now carry a third node/port-discovery path; `status.sh` runs its own `squeue -n nova-playable`. The design should name the mechanism it extends (or state why the general launcher cannot be) so the serving launch does not fork from both owners

findings.reason: naming the single owner of the forward shape step (constraint rows vs the `shape_inverse` least-squares step) would settle which path the keyboard controls drive and stop a third implementation.
findings.text: §2 assigns the shape-control vocabulary to `nova/equilibrium/inverse.py` + `ControlPoints` and defers the row transfer to `constraint-augmented-newton-krylov` §4, but the code now carries two forward shape-control paths for the same goal: the constraint-row route (`nova/equilibrium/constraint.py`, whose `constraint_response_matrix`, `CircuitCurrentUnknown`, `CompensatorRule` and `CurrentCentroidConstraint` are the row vocabulary) and the inverse-least-squares route already landed in `nova/equilibrium/shape_inverse.py` ("poses the same step on the forward operator's prescribed-current carrier"). §2 names neither `shape_inverse.py` nor `constraint.py`, so the playable solve can fork a third shape path rather than extend the one that exists

findings.reason: the section should either justify a nova-owned status read distinct from the tunnel's node discovery or delete it and let the serving job report through the launcher/tunnel it already depends on.
findings.text: the design's status read is a thin layer over the scheduler query (`squeue` for job/node/start) and over the allocation record the payload writes, yet §6 gives no reason the tunnel's `discover_compute_node` (which §6 itself relies on for the tunnel's remote end) cannot supply node/port, nor why the general lane launcher cannot host the log/status contract. A wrapper with no such justification is the parallel path the duplicate_owner finding names

findings.reason: with every family's budget at zero the design must account for the interface surface it adds in its own text (name a retirement, a merge, or the reason there is none) before the surface lands.
findings.text: §6 adds a status command (a CLI), §7 adds the `--decoder`/`--machine` launch options and a `view` request argument, and §5/§7 add the `FrameDecoder`/`DecodedFrame` public definitions and the `SteeringFrame` session schema; none of these sections names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, against the week's budgets of public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. §6 even asserts "Three existing pieces compose it, none new" while delivering a new command

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the §7 `FrameDecoder` is a one-method protocol (`decode(frame) -> DecodedFrame`) that hides the whole checkpoint/VQ/corpus decoder behind the seam, and §5's session schema is one typed record the corpus, the decoder and the page all read; the design hides substantial behaviour behind small interfaces.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 adds a bespoke sbatch launcher and scheduler status read beside `scripts/nova_lane/run.sh` and imas-codex's `discover_compute_node`, and §2's control vocabulary now sits across three row owners without naming which it extends.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the design's design sections add a status command, the `--decoder`/`--machine` launch options, the `view` request argument, and the `FrameDecoder`/`DecodedFrame` public definitions, and no section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — each design section names the mechanism it extends rather than proposes fresh: §2 `nova/equilibrium/inverse.py` + `ControlPoints` (`nova/geometry/plasmapoints.py`) and the `constraint-augmented-newton-krylov` row transfer; §3 the `millisecond-converged-solve` reduced route; §4 `apps/pulsedesign/`; §6 `reckon serve` + the imas-codex tunnel; §7 imas-ambix's decoder + `equilibrium_labels.py`; §8 the §5 `SteeringFrame` and the constrained row set. The plan searched the repos it names; the two forks below are named owners, not missing searches.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 deliverable A's status command adds a fresh scheduler query over `squeue` rather than saying why the tunnel's existing node discovery cannot serve it.
